
[[File:The Sister and Witch.png|right|200px|thumb|The Sister-and-Witch]]
{{Quote|In twain, they hailed, from different fates and fortunes across the vast expanse. The Sister, radiating with the luminosity of Lantern, paved their path to endurance; the Witch, armed with the sharpness of Edge, left them restless and seeking...|Brodnax, ''Those Who Do Not Sleep''}}
'''The Sister-and-Witch''', also dubbed '''[[The Twins]]''', stands among the esteemed [[Hours]], linked with hour XVIII, or 6:00pm. She is the mirror reflection of [[The Witch-and-Sister]]. Her foremost [[Aspects]] are {{Lore|Lantern}}, {{Lore|Edge}}, and {{Lore|Knock}}.

Emerging as Gods-from-Flesh, The Twins bear a shared tale of inception. As chronicled in ''[[The Larquebine Codex]]'', their legend whispers of a genesis "from the West, birthed from contrasting destinies—one, a beacon of simplicity, and the other, a force of affluence. Yet, bound by an innate love, they converged in shadow 'in pursuit of unity'." When their realm sought to offer them in appeasement to break a relentless drought, they eluded their grim destiny, venturing across vast seas. However, the weight of their journey bore down on them, culminating in a tragic embrace of the watery abyss. Thus, through [[Way: Through the Stag Door#The Painted River|The Painted River]] and the intercession of [[The Red Grail]], they ascended into the sanctum of the [[Mansus]]. Yet, in a twist of fate described by the sage Brodnax in ''[[Those Who Do Not Sleep]]'', The Red Grail, sensing a threat in The Twins' ascending power, birthed [[The Thunderskin]] to confront them.

Links to the Sister-and-Witch are found in the tome known as ''[[The Geminiad]]'', and echoes of the archaic dialect of Fucine, once chanted by the spell-weavers near Italy's Lake Fucino.
